thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty triggered — incident PD-9731 for service=\"inference-prod\" (high error rate on /v1/generate). Currently routed to schedule: platform-oncall. Link: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-9731

pagerduty-bot: Escalation: assigned to Ben Ortiz — first responder notified.

Alex Chen: I just hopped in — looks like this should have gone to inference-oncall not platform. platform-oncall is getting paged for a model-serving error.

Maria Gomez: whoa — confirmed. PD payload shows tags: {team: \"inference\", service: \"inference-prod\"} but routing rule \"prod-servicing->platform\" matched because of an old legacy rule.

Priya Nair: @oncall-rota can you confirm current schedule ownership? I think inference-oncall is new rotation but maybe not wired into PD service.

oncall-rota: We migrated inference-oncall last month but didn't update the PD escalation entries for the old 'prod-serving' service. That explains it.

Ben Ortiz: Acked PD-9731. I'm triaging now. Quick status: 5% 5xx from EU edge to /v1/generate, latencies normal prior to error spike. Early hypothesis: model server OOM for a small subset of requests.

Alex Chen: Thanks Ben. While you triage, can someone reassign the PD incident to inference-oncall? pd-cli still requires owner change.

Maria Gomez: I can do a forced reassignment. Running:
```
pd incidents assign PD-9731 --service inference-prod --escalation inference-oncall
```
If that fails, fallback is to remove platform-oncall from escalation policy.

pagerduty-bot: Command accepted by Maria Gomez. Incident reassigned to escalation policy inference-oncall; notifying Priya Nair and Alex Chen.

Priya Nair: I got the page. I'm joining the call and pulling logs. Initial grep shows a spike in KV cache misses and repeated small-batch requests from a customer integration.

Alex Chen: Which customer? Are retries flooding? Could be a client SDK bug.

Priya Nair: Looks like customer-id: cust-92 (third-party partner). Their client sent repeated parallel requests with an empty prompt field — server-side validation returned 500 instead of 4xx. Fixing validation will stop the errors but we should mitigate now.

Ben Ortiz: Mitigation: enabling a WAF rule to drop requests missing required fields at the edge for cust-92, and enabling circuit-breaker for rapid-failure. Applying now.

Priya Nair: Also going to patch the model server to return 400 for empty prompt. Small code change, will rollout canary to 10% for 5 minutes then 100% if green.

Alex Chen: Good. Customer impact? Any SLA breaches or active customers complaining?

Priya Nair: We see 8 active API keys impacted across 5 customers. cust-92 accounts for ~60% of error volume. No support tickets yet but we should notify CSMs.

Maria Gomez: I'll open a quick customer notif draft. Proposed: "We're investigating elevated error rates affecting some inference requests; mitigations in progress. We'll follow up with a root cause and ETA."

Ben Ortiz: Mitigations applied: WAF rule active, circuit-breaker engaged. Errors dropped to baseline in last 45s. PD-9731 marked as mitigated by Ben Ortiz.

incident-bot: Incident PD-9731: status changed to \"Mitigated\" by Ben Ortiz.

Priya Nair: Rolling the validation patch now. Canary looks clean. Promoting to 100% in 2 mins.

Alex Chen: Nice. Follow-up items before close: 1) Remove legacy PD routing rule mapping prod-serving -> platform. 2) Add integration tests for prompt validation to avoid 500s. 3) Notify customers + CSMs. 4) Postmortem owned by Maria.

Maria Gomez: I'll own the postmortem. Will also file a PD change request to update service->escalation mappings.

Ben Ortiz: Leaving a note on rotation: platform-oncall got noisy page; apologies to platform team — we'll add a PD runbook entry to verify service mappings on rotation changes.

Alex Chen: Thanks all. Handing off to Maria for post-incident follow-up. Marking thread resolved in Slack once postmortem link is up. :thumbsup:

Maria Gomez: Postmortem draft link: https://redwood.atlassian.com/pm/PD-9731-postmortem — will circulate for comments.

incident-bot: Thread closed by Maria Gomez.
